related_resources.reason: Historical origination of the mountain-pass approach to non-minimizing variational critical points.
Minimax path geometry and deformation mechanism.
Vocabulary for the path minimax idea.

historical_claims.claim: Ambrosetti and Rabinowitz developed the mountain-pass critical-point framework in their 1973 paper.

authorship.scope: Original audio-first lecture and mathematical companion on nonlinear minimax, Palais–Smale compactness, explicit semilinear existence, or critical exponent scaling; inherited manuscripts are unchanged.

prerequisites.reason: Know how an energy assigns a number to a function and how to compute a first variation.
Contrast the direct method for minimizers with non-minimizing critical points.

recommended.reason: Review norms, completeness and Hilbert-space methods before variational compactness.
Contrast stationary nonlinear boundary problems with evolution equations.

background: Single-variable critical points, basic multivariable derivatives, integration by parts, function norms and weak solutions; the new path-minimax arguments are developed from examples.
readiness_checks: Locate all critical points of one-half x squared minus one-quarter x to the fourth and classify them.
Explain why every path in the plane from (0,0) to (2,0) must reach energy at least one quarter.

description: Examines accessible energy landscapes, non-minimizing critical points, path minimax, and the transition from scalar calculus to a function-valued unknown.
